name: media-split-stack-section
purpose: A run of large media-split bands that pile up under the site header as the page scrolls, each a centered claim with an outlined "learn more" button beside its picture, the whole band linking through. An optional centered section title at the medium size opens the run, as the run headers of the live product pages do. It is a page section — the site places it from a `{ _id: 'media-split-stack-section', props }` entry and binds `props` straight onto it — and it composes `module`, `module-header`, `split-stack`, `media-split`, `illustration`, `console-mockup` and `button`. Every band has a picture, and it is a drawn asset: a registered `scene`, a `ConsoleMockup` console mock (`widget`, itself a registered scene), or a registry `illustration`. The band type is a union that requires one of them; request-flow diagrams and code do not go in a media band. Every band sets its picture at the closing end, so the run reads down one edge.
useWhen: Use MediaSplitStackSection for a run of linked claims that pile up as the reader scrolls.
To list the solution areas or the claims of a page, one large band each, with a link through to its own page.
avoidWhen: For a single claim beside its picture or scene → use `media-split-section`.
For a request-flow diagram → use `console-showcase-section` with `variant: 'diagram'`; for code → use `feature-scroll-section`.
For small reasons in a grid → use `feature-tiles-section`.
related: `split-stack` — the sticky run the bands pile up in.
`media-split` — the band each entry renders through.
bestPractices: Give every band one picture: `scene`, `widget` (a `ConsoleMockup` name — the product's console screen), or `illustration` (a name of the illustration registry, with `illustrationLabel`); a band takes no picture URL. The type requires one; when several are set the first in that order wins. Page JSON is untyped, so a band with none renders without its media cell, logs a development warning, and fails the site-composition check (`test/standards/site-composition.test.mjs`). A `Diagram` scene counts as none.
Give every band an `action`; it is both the button and the link the whole band follows.

props.name: anchor
props.doc: In-page id set on the run so a `#hash` link can scroll to it.

props.name: title
props.doc: Headline of the run, rendered by the medium centered section title as its `h2`; the run renders no header when empty, and with a header each band's headline drops to an `h3`.

props.name: description
props.doc: Supporting sentence under the section title.

props.name: bands
props.doc: The bands, in order; each is `{ title, description, eyebrow?, href?, action? }` plus its required picture, one of `scene`, `widget` or `illustration` (with `illustrationLabel?`), where `eyebrow` is the band's overline, `href` the link the whole band follows (falling back to the action's), `scene` a webkit scene asset other than `Diagram`, `widget` a `ConsoleMockup` name, `illustration` a name of the illustration registry, and `action` `{ label, href }` the outlined button.
